A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GraphUniverse and are readable throughout, including equations, figures, tables, and all appendices. The shared methodology and experiments can be matched despite the revised title, added sections, and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-generation validation, timing measurements, architecture benchmarks, distribution-shift experiments, and graph-size generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds real-world dataset alignment experiments and evaluations of heterophily-specialized architectures.

M1.justification: The implemented hierarchical generator is retained. Appendix D.1.1 newly specifies a prospective overlapping-community variant using co-occurrence distributions, a mixing matrix, weighted edge probabilities, and mixed feature centroids. This is a limited proposed extension, explicitly not established as implemented or evaluated.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic community detection and triangle counting. v2 adds native-task evaluation on OGBG-MolHIV, AQSOL, NCI1, IMDB-MULTI, and ZINC, together with corresponding synthetic datasets. Section 5.5, Table 4, and the alignment figures establish substantial new molecular and social-network coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix L and Figure 12 add FAGCN, H2GCN, and ChebNet as evaluated comparators, substantially extending the architectural comparison to heterophily-specialized approaches. Figure 12 omits TopoTune, although the original nine-model comparisons remain in Figures 3 and 4.

E3.justification: The new real-world comparison matches GraphUniverse property ranges to dataset percentiles and GraphWorld parameters to means, using 1000-node GraphWorld graphs. Models solve native tasks on real data and community detection on synthetic data. Appendix L adds a five-point transductive homophily sweep. Table 1 also expands the graph-size timing sweep and removes R-squared reporting.

E4.justification: v2 adds synthetic-to-real performance and ranking alignment analyses, including comparisons with and without DeepSet and GraphMLP to examine correlation inflation. Appendix L tests whether specialized heterophily advantages persist inductively. These are substantive additions beyond the retained parameter-sensitivity, distribution-shift, and size-generalization analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix K adds 1000-iteration bootstrap rank estimation, bootstrap standard-deviation error bars, and rank-correlation p-values. The existing three-data-seed performance reporting remains; bootstrap iterations are not additional training runs. The reported timing average changes from 500 graphs in v1 to 100 in v2.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive real-world alignment and specialized-model results. For example, Figure 10 reports OGBG-MolHIV rank correlations of 0.771 for GraphUniverse and -0.143 for GraphWorld after excluding non-message-passing baselines. Table 1 replaces timing estimates, including 0.020 to 0.023 seconds for 100-node graphs, under changed averaging conditions; this is not a controlled performance deterioration.

T1.justification: Appendix D.1.1 adds formal membership-vector definitions and equations for overlapping-community edge probabilities, degree-factor selection, and feature generation. The earlier Bernoulli–Poisson correspondence, scaling derivations, and validation-metric definitions are retained after renumbering. No new proof establishes the proposed extension's claimed properties.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 3 newly claims that GraphUniverse datasets can serve as effective real-world proxies through correlated model rankings. The conclusion also narrows foundation-model applications to potential extensions requiring further development. The original claims about inductive evaluation and context-dependent robustness remain.

C2.justification: New Appendices B and D explicitly discuss unvalidated foundation-model applications, realistic feature fitting, community-identification difficulties, inability to control motifs or geometry, and possible bias toward community-structured models. New interpretations address synthetic-to-real transfer and why heterophily-specific advantages may diminish inductively.

D1.justification: v1 promises release upon acceptance; v2 reports available PyPI/GitHub resources, TopoBench integration, and local demo deployment. It adds dataset-to-generator extraction instructions, specialized-model search grids, and default sum pooling. Conversely, the default-parameter table removes the degree-heterogeneity and Use DCCC-SBM rows; this does not establish an underlying implementation change.

R1.justification: Related work and Appendix B substantially broaden positioning through CGT, metadata-driven synthetic evaluation, GraphFM, OpenGraph, and synthetic-data precedents in vision and language. These additions develop relationships to dataset matching and foundation-model augmentation beyond v1's principal comparisons with GraphWorld and static benchmarks. Publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: The title and publication header change, model descriptions are compressed, and selected introductory, validation, and concluding passages are revised. New research-question, discussion, reproducibility, and acknowledgment sections are inserted, but the original narrative order and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds alignment and heterophily displays, extracted-parameter and specialized-model tables, and reorganizes legends, colors, and appendix layouts. Table 1 gains size rows and loses its R-squared column. Figure 11 visibly duplicates Figure 10 despite a caption claiming inclusion of additional baselines, introducing a substantive presentation error.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens a central weakness of v1: its validation was entirely synthetic. The five-dataset alignment study, specialized-architecture checks, explicit applicability limits, and reported code availability improve evidential support and reproducibility. Reporting problems qualify these gains: Figure 11 duplicates Figure 10, and uniformly superior alignment is overstated, since IMDB-MULTI rank correlation without baselines is 0.543 versus GraphWorld's 0.600. These localized weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial new validation and clearer boundaries.
